card.name: Multi-drug dosing instructions, word before drug names
card.fires_on: Words in dosing instructions that involve more than one drug or component, such as 'used' in 'more than one topical ophthalmic drug is being used', or 'dosage' or 'component' when a combination product is being adjusted.

modes.label: More than one eye drug
modes.description: The word 'used' or 'be used' in the instruction about using several topical ophthalmic products together.
modes.example: If more than one topical ophthalmic drug is being<< used>>, the drugs should be administered at least

modes.label: Combination product dose wording
modes.description: Words that refer to the dose or part of a two-drug product when switching or adjusting.
modes.example: Select a dosage that is as close as possible to the current<< dosage>> of pioglitazone and met

modes.label: Inside combo drug names
modes.description: Partway through a drug name or brand name within a combination product.
modes.example: or any of the excipients in SOLI<<QU>>A 100/33

card.writes: It leans away from words meaning 'combine' and toward words like 'each', 'a set of' and 'distributed'.
card.plain: It marks spots in label text where two or more drugs are being used together and the instructions refer to each one.
